title: Predict: Mutating Structs in a Loop
hints: `for var p in array` gives you a copy of each struct.
Mutating the copy doesn't change the array; mutating `players[i]` does. Class elements are shared references.
jsBridge: `for var item in items` gives you a **copy** of each struct, so mutating it doesn't touch the array. In JS, `for (const o of arr) o.x = 1` mutates the shared objects. To mutate in place in Swift, loop over indices or use `for i in items.indices`.

compass.q: In JS mutating loop items changes the array's objects. Why doesn't Swift, and how do you write the in-place version?
`items.indices` loop vs `items = items.map { … }` vs `for i in 0..<items.count`: which is idiomatic?
What if the elements are class instances? Does `for item in items { item.x = 1 }` mutate?
`ForEach($items) { $item in … }` in SwiftUI binds each element. How does that solve this problem for UI?
